chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_changelog.py::_entries (bug loop, `field["category"]`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The module docstring and the stated intent both promise that "an entry whose field says `skip` / `internal` is left out", but the code only tests `field.get("skip")`:
```
field = it.changelog or {}
if field.get("skip"):
    continue
```
Nothing anywhere in `_entries`, `_row`, or `build_sections` handles an `internal` marker. For a done task (or bug) whose changelog field marks it internal — e.g. `changelog = {"category": "internal", "line": "Rework internal retry loop"}` or `changelog = {"internal": true, "line": ...}` — the guard is false, so the entry is emitted; `_row` then coerces the unknown category to `"Changed"` (`category if category in CHANGELOG_CATEGORIES else "Changed"`), so the internal entry silently leaks into `## [Unreleased]` under Changed rather than being suppressed as specified.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_changelog.py::_entries (skip check, `if field.get("skip")`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture deliberately tags the very commit it calls "old work": `shas["c0"] = commit(..., "old work", ...)` is immediately followed by `git tag -a v1.0.0`, so `v1.0.0` points at c0, and item `B-old` carries `merged_sha == c0` with `completed_at = 2026-09-06`. Under the intent ("Version of an item: git ancestry of merged_sha against tags … nothing is reconstructed before the first tag"), an item whose merge commit is contained in the first tag has version 1.0.0 — c0 is *in* v1.0.0, not *before* it. Yet the expected output drops it entirely: GOLDEN contains no `## [1.0.0]` section, `B-old`/"Old work" is absent, and `test_skip_suppresses_and_baseline_stays_out` asserts `"[1.0.0]" not in body`. This is internally contradictory: the preamble the golden itself asserts says "nothing before v1.0.0 is reconstructed", which promises the 1.0.0 release is present, while the body omits it. Concretely, for a repo whose history is `c0 -> tag v1.0.0 -> c1,c2,c3 -> tag v1.1.0 -> c4,c5`, a user gets a changelog with no record of the first release at all, and `test_compare_links_from_origin_and_tags` bakes this in by asserting the body ends at the `[1.1.0]: …/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0` link, i.e. no `[1.0.0]` link exists either. Under any rule consistent with the stated ancestry semantics c0 must land in *some* release (either v1.0.0, the first tag containing it, or v1.1.0 under a strictly-after rule), so dropping it is a behavioral defect, not a legitimate reading of "before the first tag".
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_changelog.py::GOLDEN (and test_skip_suppresses_and_baseline_stays_out / test_compare_links_from_origin_and_tags)

chunk_findings.detail: For a fixed bug the code requires only `field.get("line")` and then reads the category with a hard index: `rows.append(_row(bug.id, field["category"], ...))`. The task path deliberately uses `field.get("category") or _category(...)` (with a final `"Fixed"/"Changed"` fallback), which shows the `changelog` field's category is optional. So a bug whose field carries a line but no category — e.g. `changelog = {"line": "Fix the parser crash"}` — reaches line `field["category"]` and raises `KeyError: 'category'`, aborting the whole export instead of falling back to `Changed`/`Fixed` as the documented rule "1. explicit changelog field's category … 5. Changed" requires. Note `_row` would already normalize an unknown category, so the hard index is gratuitous.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_changelog.py:_entries (bug loop, `field["category"]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring says "An entry whose field says `skip` / `internal` is left out." The task loop implements this (`if field.get("skip"): continue`), but the bug loop's guard is only `if not bug.fixed_at or not field.get("line") or bug.id in named: continue` — there is no `skip` test. Given a fixed bug with `changelog = {"line": "internal cleanup", "category": "Fixed", "skip": True}`, it is not named by any task, so it passes the guard and is emitted into the changelog, contradicting the stated suppression rule. The two loops handle the same field and should apply the same suppression.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_changelog.py:_entries (bug loop, missing skip check)

chunk_findings.detail: The test creates a branch tip `tip` and even asserts `tip != m`, but the event that drives the version logic uses `sha=m` — the merge commit on `main` — not `tip`. The docstring claims to verify "a landing whose merge commit is on main only is found by its branch tip on another line", yet no event ever supplies the branch tip as `merged_sha`. As a result, an implementation of `reached()` that resolves only merge commits (and not a branch tip that was merged in) would still pass this test. The concrete untested input is an item whose `merged_sha` is `tip` (a commit reachable only through a merge commit's second parent); if the implementation mishandled that case, the test suite would not catch it.
